rationale: Cheap RF jamming of an unauthenticated C2 link forces fail-safe or crash during BVLOS, with intercepted MAVLink adding full situational compromise.
A trivially scriptable signature bypass grants unrestricted flight authorisation, collapsing the trust anchor the whole U-plan service rests on.
Vendor-level firmware backdooring is resource-intensive and hard to detect without SBOM or signing, but compromises every deployed airframe at once.
Tailgating into a vertiport sabotages control panels and landing zones, but impact is confined to one facility and physical repetition is difficult.
Audit-log tampering at the regulator erodes oversight and enforcement across operators without causing direct airborne harm.
Automated SQL injection against an unpatched USSP database is easy to find and repeat, yielding mass exfiltration and corruption of flight records.
Leaked strategic plans and risk registers are an intelligence enabler for later attacks rather than an operational or safety event.
Debug-port and unsigned-update abuse gives full flight-controller control, but needs physical or build-chain access per target model.
Injected geofence boundaries steer every subscribing operator in a volume toward restricted airspace while appearing legitimate.
Phantom tracks and masked real conflicts degrade separation for all traffic monitored by the service, raising mid-air collision risk.
A stolen key with no rate limiting enables trivially repeatable bulk exfiltration, but the harm is confidentiality rather than flight safety.
Poisoning the single source of truth propagates corrupted state simultaneously to every dependent U-space service with no integrity check to stop it.
Weak identity proofing lets unaccountable operators fly legally-looking missions, undermining attribution more than immediate safety.
Unsecured write access allows deletion of no-fly records, silently opening restricted airspace to every operator consuming the database.
Manipulated third-party weather and traffic feeds cause unsafe routing region-wide, though tactical deconfliction partially mitigates the outcome.
Exploiting legislative ambiguity to skip a cybersecurity management system weakens the whole ecosystem's baseline without being an attack in itself.
Low-cost, well-documented GNSS spoofing and jamming defeat an unauthenticated single-source dependency and affect every airframe in the RF footprint.
Deleting non-immutable logs conceals incidents and blocks forensics, but requires privileged access and causes no direct operational harm.
Ground-station power loss halts local operations and BMS manipulation can deplete a battery in flight, though reach is limited to targeted assets.
Commodity DDoS against a single unprotected gateway denies authorisation services to an entire volume, typically forcing contingency landings rather than loss of control.
Signal and IMU injection corrupts flight decisions where no cross-sensor validation exists, but needs proximity and research-grade technique.
